newsitem.title: FRANCE: Israeli settlements threaten Mideast peace-Arafat.
newsitem.headline: Israeli settlements threaten Mideast peace-Arafat.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat said on Friday the building of Israeli settlements in Palestinian territories threatened Middle East peace and urged the world to save the peace process.
Arafat, addressing a Paris seminar in tribute to the late French president Francois Mitterrand, said the settlements were making the principle of land for peace an empty slogan.
Accusing hardline Israeli premier Benjamin Netanyahu of procrastinating on implementing the accords on Palestinian autonomy, he said the world should be aware of the danger.
"Peace is in danger. We must act to save the peace process from collapsing."
Peace talks have faltered since Netanyahu came to power and are deadlocked over an Israeli troop redeployment from Hebron and dates for further pullbacks in the occupied West Bank.
But both Arafat and former Israeli premier Shimon Peres voiced confidence that Israelis and Palestinians would reach agreement as both recognised peace was their only option.
"What we have solved so far is an indication of what we can solve in the future," Peres said.

Arafat and Peres, the architects of the Oslo accords, embraced warmly before taking their seats at the seminar at the UNESCO headquarters, with Peres referring to Arafat in French as "mon ami" (my friend).

Both paid tribute to Mitterrand as a pioneer of Middle East peace who saw through the complexities of Middle East conflict, and voiced confidence, as Mitterrand had, that peace would prevail despite the current difficulties in the peace process.
"(Mitterrand) was sure the peace agreement would gather force and neither of the two sides would have the strength to pull it down," Peres said.

Arafat recalled Mitterrand's ground-breaking speech to the Knesset in 1982, when he called on Israel to open dialogue with the Palestinian Liberation Organisation (PLO), and Arafat's official audience at the French presidential palace in 1989.
"(Mitterrand) was one of these great politicians whose realism can turn a dream into a vision," he said.
Peres recalled that Mitterrand warned him against continued occupation of Palestinian territories, telling him: "Don't think you can have an enlightened occupation".
He said the late French leader had been careful throughout his 14-year rule to alienate neither Israelis nor Palestinians.

The former Israeli Labour leader, a long-time friend of the Socialist Mitterrand, emotionally concluded: "We will always cherish a man who could see the morrow of our lives and see that the future is a consequence of the future rather than a continuation of the past."
